summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -7 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar −; brl −; mxn −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +4.7%; weakest: Lean hogs -21.2%. Key releases ahead: US Core PCE Price Index m/m (11-25 8:30 AM ET); US Prelim GDP q/q (11-25 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.91% (-9 bp in a month), 2-year 4.63% (-6 bp); 2s10s curve +28 bp (-3 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.17% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.99 (+2.0% in a month, +5.8% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.902 (+19.0% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.662 (-0.2%); USD/MXN 19.70 (+5.2%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -5.5% in a month (+5.2% YTD); VIX 30.8. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 82.21 $/bbl (-17.4% in a month), Brent 88.93, ULSD 3.659 $/gal (-21.0%), natural gas 3.61 (+2.7%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -18.8% in a month, Shanghai Composite -6.0%, Hang Seng -5.4%, yuan +0.2% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 10 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (30%); S&P GSCI -14.8% in a month; gold -12.9%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.

events_ahead.title: Core PCE Price Index m/m
